sections.html:
In Marysville you may hire a broker, track down a buyer on your own, or accept a plain cash purchase. The route changes, but the deed paperwork still lands at the Union County auditor and recorder.

Match the house's condition to your calendar. Listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings and an inspection report. A cash offer leaves a single negotiation over price and closing day.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, at the cost of a commission and repair haggling.
  • Owner-run: no commission, but all the marketing and contract work is yours.
  • Cash: one number, fewer steps and often your pick of closing day.

Marysville has an estimated 30,190 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,571 in the April 2020 count. That is growth of 17.9 percent since the 2020 estimates base, and it has kept demand for houses steady.

The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $300,800 for 2020-2024, and owners live in 67.5 percent of units. Rent has a median of $1,223 a month, and owner costs have medians of $1,851 with a mortgage and $681 without one. The city has 10,163 households averaging 2.46 people, and median household income is $92,619.

Citywide medians say little about one address. Ask for a written review of recent sales near yours before you accept any number.

The Union County seat sits roughly 27 miles northwest of Columbus, and its employers keep a steady stream of buyers nearby. Scotts Miracle-Gro was founded here in 1868 and still has its headquarters in the city. Honda's Marysville Auto Plant, about six miles northwest, has built the Accord since 1982. Nestle, Univenture and a Parker Hannifin plant add more jobs.

U.S. Route 33 runs four lanes through town, tying it to Interstate 75 and the I-270 outerbelt. Tree-lined streets earned the city the nickname Shaded City, and more than 300 acres of parks hold trails along Mill Creek. The Union County Fair runs from late July into early August.

Timberview, an upscale section with a golf course, and Greenwood Colony sit on the south side, and the Uptown square holds the library and city offices.

Marysville gets 40.48 inches of precipitation and 24.0 inches of snow in a typical year. January lows average 20.6 degrees Fahrenheit, and the all-time record high is 109. Roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces absorb those swings each year, which is why an inspector looks at them first.

When one of those is nearly worn out, tell buyers at the start. Cash buyers simply price the work in; financed buyers bring it up after inspection.

Almost all of Marysville falls in the Marysville Exempted Village School District, with a few parcels reaching into Fairbanks Local. The district changes your tax bill, so verify it for the parcel.

The Union County auditor's GIS map includes a school district layer. If a district line cuts through a house, the district holding the master bedroom taxes the entire house. The auditor's parcel page has a "Where your taxes go" link that lists every levy and a Total Effective Rate, which is the quickest way to see the rate for your address.

sections.h2: What a Marysville seller must disclose
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure duty for houses with up to four units. The seller completes the state form, signs and dates it, and hands it to prospective buyers. It asks about water supply, sewage, roof and foundation, radon, lead paint, asbestos and other known defects.

The duty does not reach every transfer. Excluded sales include:

  • Court-ordered transfers and fiduciary transfers for an estate or trust.
  • Transfers to a spouse or direct-line relatives.
  • Heirs who never lived in the house during the previous year.

A buyer handed the form late may cancel in writing for three business days after receiving it. That right lapses 30 days after acceptance or at closing, if sooner.

Ohio Revised Code 5301.01 has the seller sign the deed and acknowledge it before a notary or similar officer. The deed then goes to the Union County Auditor at 233 W. Sixth St. in Marysville, where the buyer's side files a value statement (DTE 100) or an exemption statement (DTE 100EX).

The seller settles the conveyance fee, so ask the auditor which rate applies before closing day. Mailed conveyances reach the recorder only with the auditor's stamp already applied. The recorder charges $39.00 for a deed through page two, then $8.00 a page.

A Board of Revision complaint on a Union County parcel must reach the auditor after January 1 and on or before March 31. The other deadlines and amounts are below.

Union County deadlines and fees for Marysville owners
ActionDeadline or amount
Board of Revision complaintReceived after January 1 and on or before March 31
Appeal of a board decisionThirty days from the decision letter, filed with the Board of Tax Appeals (DTE Form 4) or Common Pleas Court
Homestead exemption, change in statusNotify the auditor by the first Monday in June
Refund after a value cutDecisions wait 30 days, then adjustments follow in about sixty days
Deed recording$39.00 first two pages, $8.00 each added page
  • The 2.5 percent rollback covers owner-occupied homes, one property per owner, and requires an application.
  • A requested change above $50,000 of market value, or $17,500 assessed, sends notice to the school board.
  • After a recent sale, attach the closing statement, contract and deed to support your complaint.

Marysville requires a zoning permit for most additions: decks, fences, swimming pools, sheds, garages and room additions, plus public sidewalks and driveway approaches built by a contractor registered with the city. Some jobs also need a building permit from the Union County Building Department.

Ask the city zoning office about any structure on your lot that lacks one. Old decks and sheds show up on inspections, and a cash buyer will price in whatever cleanup remains.

A cash sale suits owners who value a quick, certain close over the last few thousand dollars of price. Common cases:

  • An inherited house nobody plans to occupy.
  • An aging roof, furnace or foundation.
  • Tenants who make showings hard to schedule.
  • A job move on a fixed date.

Set any offer beside what a listing would leave you after repair bills, commission and months of upkeep. A cash buyer also skips the lender's appraisal, so a low appraisal cannot pull the price down late in the process.

Plan on three things in the last week: a signed and notarized deed, the value or exemption statement for the auditor, and a payoff letter if a mortgage remains. A title company can carry the deed to the Union County Auditor and then to the recorder, and it will list any taxes still owed on your settlement statement. Keep copies of the disclosure form and anything else you handed the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marysville house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale, but problems you know about belong on the disclosure form. A cash purchaser accepts the house as found, while a buyer with a lender may ask for fixes.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Marysville sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the grantor settles it before the auditor endorses the deed.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Marysville property value?
faqs.a: Union County takes these complaints from January 1 to March 31, for the current tax year only. A notarized complaint goes to the auditor by email, fax or mail.

faqs.q: Does an inherited Marysville house need the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Frequently not. Transfers by an estate's fiduciary are excluded, as are sales by heirs who never occupied the house in the previous year.

faqs.q: How do I find the tax rate for a Marysville parcel?
faqs.a: Look up the parcel on the Union County auditor's website. The Total Effective Rate column under "Where your taxes go" gives the rate for that district.
